identity.title: AgentGym-RL: An Open-Source Framework to Train LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Decision Making via Multi-Turn RL

problem.claim: Train LLM agents for complex, multi-turn and long-horizon decision-making through extensive environment exploration and reinforcement learning.

gap.claim: Open-source tooling lacks a unified framework for training agents from scratch across diverse, realistic environments; vanilla long-horizon training also encounters instability.

contributions.claim: Introduces AgentGym-RL, a modular, decoupled framework supporting mainstream RL algorithms across broad real-world scenarios.
Proposes ScalingInter-RL, which stages training from short-horizon interactions toward progressively deeper exploration for more stable long-horizon RL training.
Releases the framework, code, and datasets for community use.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their framework by combining modularity and decoupling with broad environment coverage, and distinguish their training approach through staged horizon expansion.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their trained agents perform on par with or surpass commercial counterparts including OpenAI o3 and Gemini-2.5-Pro across 27 tasks in diverse environments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex multi-turn decision-making requires extensive environmental exploration, making RL a natural training route.
The open-source community lacks a unified framework spanning from-scratch training and diverse realistic environments; long-horizon vanilla training is also unstable.
The paper introduces AgentGym-RL as a flexible, extensible framework and ScalingInter-RL as a staged strategy that expands interaction horizons.
The authors report parity with or superiority to named commercial systems on 27 diverse tasks, alongside a code-and-dataset release.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a concrete training challenge—long-horizon instability—with a specific staged intervention that begins at short horizons and expands them progressively.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the proposed mechanism legible by mapping the intervention directly to the stated failure mode.
lessons.application: When presenting a long-horizon training method, explicitly pair each difficulty with the corresponding training-stage change and its intended role.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has no staged mechanism or when the abstract cannot identify a specific target failure mode.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide algorithmic details, baselines beyond the named commercial systems, task-level results, statistical variation, or ablations.
The reported comparison conditions and the meaning of “performance” are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independently verified effectiveness, novelty, or reproducibility.
